skills.name: agile-work-hierarchy
skills.description: Use when planning, creating, reviewing, or reconciling Agile work as an Epic or Milestone → Feature → User Story → Task hierarchy, with independent Bugs and separate dependencies, in Linear, GitHub Issues, Azure DevOps, or Jira.

provenance.notes: Original user-defined Agile work hierarchy based on Graph Engineering, with independent Bugs, portable provider projections, and a local plan validator. Official provider documentation checked on 2026-10-29; native mappings require target-specific capability discovery.

versions.expectedBehavior: Plans, reviews, or reconciles Agile work as an Epic or Milestone → Feature → User Story → Task hierarchy with independent Bugs and separate dependency edges. Drafts by default and changes a tracker only with authorization; the bundled validator checks plan structure (exit 0 valid, 1 violations, 2 usage error).

skills.name: enterprise-agent-architecture
skills.description: Use when designing, reviewing, or documenting governed enterprise AI agents (knowledge, diagnostic, or action agents and multi-agent systems): capability contracts, source authority tiers, hybrid retrieval, tool permissions and approval gates, risk-tiered governance, audit, and evaluation. Covers choosing among Microsoft Agent Framework, Google ADK, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, and LangGraph.

provenance.notes: User-supplied Enterprise Agent Architecture guide contributed under Apache-2.0; unavailable long-form reference pointers removed for a self-contained import. Framework-specific claims require current primary-source verification.

versions.expectedBehavior: Guides design and review of governed enterprise AI agents through the eight pillars, source authority tiers, hybrid retrieval and risk-tiered governance. Produces design documents or ranked reviews that separate proposed controls from implemented ones, and checks framework claims against current documentation.

skills.name: graph-engineering
skills.description: Use when designing, reviewing, or refactoring AI agent workflows into explicit execution graphs: branches, parallel workers, approvals, retries, stateful handoffs, or slow and flaky agent loops. Prefer a script for simple sequential work.

provenance.notes: User-supplied Graph Engineering runbook contributed under Apache-2.0; the unverified publication-attribution caveat is preserved in SKILL.md.

versions.expectedBehavior: Turns agent workflows into explicit execution graphs (node contracts, routers, gates, bounded loops, checkpoints) or reviews existing ones, leading with ranked findings. Recommends a plain script when a graph is not needed and stays framework-neutral unless one is chosen.

skills.name: grill-with-docs
skills.description: Use when asked to grill a plan, stress-test a design, or clarify and document a domain model in one session: interview in dependency-aware rounds with recommendations, keeping a domain glossary and qualifying architecture decision records. For multi-session planning, use Wayfinder.

provenance.notes: Portable adaptation of Matt Pocock skills with required interview/domain-modeling guidance included locally; upstream MIT notice retained.

versions.expectedBehavior: Interviews the user in dependency-aware rounds with recommendations to settle a plan or design in one session, maintaining a domain glossary and qualifying ADRs. Points multi-session planning to Wayfinder and does not treat the interview as authorization to implement.

skills.name: wayfinder
skills.description: Use when charting a route, resolving planning decisions, or resuming a Wayfinder map for a large, uncertain multi-session effort. Keeps decision tickets, a destination, fog, and a resume packet. One-session decisions: use grill-with-docs.

provenance.notes: Portable adaptation of Matt Pocock skills with required interview/domain-modeling guidance included locally; upstream MIT notice retained.

versions.expectedBehavior: Charts and maintains a multi-session decision map: destination, separate decision tickets, frontier, fog, and a resume packet. Plans only, never implements, and points decisions that fit one session to grill-with-docs.
